experiment.claim: Issue #349 -- NOT a spec claim (no deglitch or reset-pulse-width target exists anywhere in spec/; design/por_output_chain.md and DR-003 Sec8 both defer any such number). Closes the second clause of the characterization report's gap 3: por_output_chain previously had NO cell-level record at all -- it was exercised only inside the whole-block campaigns (E9-E11, E14), where its behaviour is mixed with the non-physical solver branches those campaigns report, and its deglitch delay, RESETn asserted level and short-pulse behaviour were measured nowhere on their own. This experiment drives the UNCHANGED design/por_output_chain.sym from ideal comparator and bias inputs (a constant 1 uA into IBIAS, one POR_RAW PWL: a sub-deglitch pulse first, a settle gap, then the real trip) at every point of the full 45-point PVT matrix and records, per point: the delay from the POR_RAW trip to RESETn's release, the absolute release time, the released and asserted RESETn levels, and rail-band physicality guards on the four internal nodes (TIM, NDG, TRIP, RSTB) that carry the deglitch/one-shot mechanism. The sub-deglitch pulse is rejected BY CONSTRUCTION of the stimulus ordering -- the real trip is the last edge, so a release delayed by the normal deglitch time after the trip proves the earlier pulse contributed nothing -- and the release-delay window excludes a glitch-honoring reading outright (it would precede the trip and read negative). The 1 uA ideal bias is the same convention sim/iq-top's ideal-bias variant uses and is in the range bias_core actually delivers (0.78-1.2 uA across the matrix, sim/bias-core-startup and the glitch-top delivered-bias measurement); it is NOT the shared-bias assembly, and nothing here claims the cell behaves identically under real bias_core drive.

pdk.fleet_pin_limit: an equal open_pdks commit is not proof that the runner's model library is byte-identical to this host's -- it identifies the open_pdks build, not a hash of the `sky130.lib.spice` the runner loaded, and the only model-library hash a klt report carries (`environment.models_lib_sha256`) is client-scope (`models_lib_sha256_scope: "client"`), taken on the submitting host, so it is not fleet-side evidence about the runner's library

spread_checks.note: Corner-blindness guard, same convention as sim/bias-core-startup/'s own vref spread check: if every corner returns the same release delay, the .lib/.temp injection is not taking effect. The delay is set by current-starved charging of CDG/CTIM against corner- and temperature-dependent thresholds and a supply-dependent gate overdrive, so its spread across a 5x3x3 matrix should be far above this 100 us floor; 100 us is also 1/5 of the smallest release_delay window width, so a corner-blind harness fails the spread check before any window boundary artifact could mask it.
